newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech centre-left could win nearly half seats-poll.
newsitem.headline: Czech centre-left could win nearly half seats-poll.

text.p: The ruling centre-right coalition would control 100 seats in the 200-seat Czech lower house if early elections were held, and a potential centre-left alliance would hold 97 seats, a survey showed on Thursday.

The early-June poll by the private demographics agency STEM showed Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party with 20.8 percent support of potential voters, statistically unchanged from a STEM poll in early May.

The survey showed a precarious position for Klaus's coalition -- which barely escaped being ousted earlier this week by convincing a less-than enthusiastic centrist partner, the Christian Democrats to remain on side.
The survey was conducted after the government announced tough austerity measures to counter a sharp fall in the crown which forced the central bank to float the currency on May 28.

The Klaus's pro-business coalition partner, the Civic Democratic Alliance, saw its support dip to 10 percent from 11 percent in May, while the centrist Christian Democrats rose to 13.3 percent from 12.

Under the Czech proportional election system, the coalition would maintain the same 100 seats it currently holds in the powerful lower house if the survey was reflected in an actual election, STEM said.

But support for the largest opposition party the Social Democrats grew in the June poll to 30.1 percent from 28 percent, giving a potential Christian Democrat-Social Democrat coalition, widely seen as possible by analysts, 97 total seats.
The Klaus government narrowly won a vote of confidence on Tuesday as an independent deputy voted with the coalition to save the cabinet from collapse in a 101 to 99 vote.
